eyebrow: Destinations / Africa & the Indian Ocean / Maldives
title: One island, one house
standfirst: A seaplane, a house and very little else is required.

blocks.heading: The transfer is half the decision
paras: Everything in the Maldives turns on the transfer. A badly timed seaplane costs a day at each end of the trip.
We set the seaplane window first and choose the island to fit it, rather than the other way round.

blocks.heading: Whole islands
blocks.caption: A private island, for a family or a group of friends.
paras: For eight or more people, taking a small island whole is frequently cheaper than the equivalent villas on a larger one.
It also removes the only real drawback of the Maldives, which is being on an island with other people's holidays.

blocks.heading: Under the water
blocks.caption: A dive guide held for the stay rather than by the day.
paras: The reefs vary enormously between atolls and the manta and whale shark seasons move with the monsoon.
We match the atoll to what a member wants to see, and hold the same guide for the whole stay.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: November to April is driest. May to October is quieter, greener and better value, with better odds on mantas.
No. Several islands are genuinely good for families, and a whole-island booking suits a multi-generational group better than anywhere else we work.
Seven nights. Fewer and the transfers eat the trip; more and most people want a second element.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
